title: Following the game's own hints to loot
target: How the discovery hints in R.E.P.O. are built and how to use them: what the card's colours mean, when a custom discovery is used, what makes something loot at all, and how the game decides to leave a valuable behind a monster.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A tracker or a free hand

steps.do: Read the discovery card as the game's own hint rather than as decoration, because it is built around a target and carries colours for the corners and the middle.
steps.because: the discovery graphic has a target and colours for its corners and middle (target, colorDiscoverCorner, colorDiscoverMiddle)

steps.do: Notice the other two colours a discovery can use, because there is a reminder colour and a bad colour alongside the discovery colours.
steps.because: there are reminder and bad colours as well (ColorReminderCorner, ColorReminderMiddle, ColorBadCorner, ColorBadMiddle)

steps.do: Listen as well as look, because the discovery has a sound of its own.
steps.because: the discovery graphic carries a sound (sound)

steps.do: Do not blink at the animation: it has an intro curve and a speed, so it arrives rather than appearing.
steps.because: the discovery animates in with its own curve and speed (introCurve, introSpeed)

steps.do: Expect some discoveries to be set up for a particular object, because a custom discovery can carry its own corner and middle colours and a wait before it shows.
steps.because: a custom discovery has its own colours and a wait time (ValuableDiscoverCustom, colorCorner, colorMiddle, waitTime)

steps.do: Expect that custom one to be able to sound and to be marked on the map, because both are optional parts of it.
steps.because: the custom discovery can have its own sound and map marker (hasCustomSound, customSound, hasCustomMap, customMap)

steps.do: Watch the tracker for it rather than only the screen, because a custom discovery can be marked as tracked.
steps.because: a custom discovery can be tracked (valuableTrackerTracked)

steps.do: Do not judge by looks: whether something counts as loot is decided by the game's own naming.
steps.because: whether an object counts as loot is decided by the game's own naming (ValuableObject, NotValuableObject)

steps.do: Know that loot carries presets of its own, so two things that look alike can differ in value, durability, weight and sound.
steps.because: loot carries value, durability, physics and audio presets of its own (valuePreset, durabilityPreset, physAttributePreset, audioPreset, audioPresetPitch)

steps.do: Treat something that is not loot differently, because it is given health and break thresholds instead of a value.
steps.because: a non-loot object is given health and break thresholds rather than a value (hasHealth, healthMax, healthDestroy, healthLossOnBreakLight, healthLossOnBreakMedium, healthLossOnBreakHeavy)

steps.do: Remember the game sorts loot by size, because there are volume types and a lookup for bigger or smaller ones.
steps.because: the game sorts loot by volume type and can look for bigger or smaller ones (ValuableVolume, VolumeType, LookForValuableTypes, includeBigger, includeSmaller)

steps.do: Do not assume a monster drops nothing: a monster can be set to leave a valuable behind, up to a maximum.
steps.because: a monster can be set to spawn a valuable up to a maximum (spawnValuable, spawnValuableMax)

commonMistakes: Ignoring the discovery card and hunting by eye.
Assuming two identical-looking objects are worth the same, when they carry their own presets.
Picking up something that is not loot and finding it has a health bar rather than a value.
Leaving a monster before the roll that decides whether it drops a valuable.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. The grounding for each step is listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
